institutionName: Institut d'études politiques de Paris (Sciences Po)

questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Academic opportunities

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: Wanting to learn French, had heard Sciences Po is a great university, and wanted to come to Paris.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: It was easy. I was provided with all the information needed.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: The administration at Sciences Po was very helpful in letting me switch courses so that I could obtain a place in a course that was mandatory per request from my home university.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: It was surprisingly easy. I found it through Lodgis Agency which I can recommend.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: They should know that one might experience problems with one's accommodation. For instance, I had an infestation of mice in my apartment which the agency luckily helped me find a solution for.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: The registration process begins at a certain date and time slot where all Sciences Po students have to log in online to sign up for their different courses.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: Sciences Po e-mailed and held two Zoom-meetings concerning the course registration process which I thought was sufficient information.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: I was not succesful in registering for one of my classes. I have only myself, however, to blame for this as I entered the online registration five minutes late because I had misunderstood the scheduled time slot.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: I would advice them to be ready at least fifteen minutes before the course registration begins in order to make sure that they are granted access to their preferred courses.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA classes while you were on exchange *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: The level of the courses corresponded to the level that I am used to from my bachelor studies at Copenhagen University.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: The style of teaching was different from UCPH because it was more formalised and there were not nearly as many seminars for discussing/training exercises as I am used to.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer: European Integration and Its Challenges, Comparative Politics, European Economic Law, Global Social Policy and Principles of Finance.

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I would recommend Global Social Policy. Great teacher and interesting syllabus.

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: I had to change the battery on my phone as well as pay for some slight repairs on my computer.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: Grocery prices were higher than I had expected; the same with public transportation. However, restaurant visits were much cheaper than I had expected - you can get a great pho, Chinese dish or sushi menu for just 10-15 euros.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Sciences Po offers all kinds of different activities ranging from sports over art classes to wine tasting classes.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I would recommend the art history class. The teacher took us to the Pompidou and showed us around the surrealist exhibition. That was a very memorable experience.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: See all of the museums - they are for free if you are under 26! Also go and visit places like Bourdeaux or Normandy.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: It was very easy - everybody was so friendly and welcoming.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: I didn't socialise with local students - mostly with international students and other Danish students.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: No, mainly the language.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: The friendly and international atmosphere of Sciences Po. In Paris and French culture more generally, it was definitely the French appreciation of the good things in life such as food, wine, art (museums, cinema) which was very inspiring to experience.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer: I would tell them that they have to prepare themselves for the course registration period, that there is a lot of work to do at Sciences Po but that it is definitely worth it and finally just to have fun and remember to take time off to experience all of the amazing restaurants, museums and places/parks that Paris has to offer!

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: Perhaps, it will be useful to know that the intro week program is by no means mandatory as well as it is very expensive. Despite of this, I still think it is worth paying the exorbitant amount of money to attend the program as i at least found some friends here that I enjoyed spending time with afterwards.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: The most rewarding part was definitely getting to live abroad in Paris for four months and getting to know people from all over the world. Besides that, it also just felt like a privilege to live in Paris for four months.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: The greatest challenge was probably getting everything in order by finding an apartment, completing all of the steps in Mobility Online etc. before my arrival in Paris. Besides that, I don´t think I had that many challenges.

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
